Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
1024 AM EDT Sun Aug 9 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A brief reprieve from t-storms today and turning hotter. T-storm 
chances return for the new workweek along with the threat for severe 
weather.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Even less t-storms today with increasing chances for the
  new workweek. Turning hotter as well with high humidity 
  continuing. 

- 2) Shower and t-storm chances remain through at least Saturday
  ahead of a cold front that will bring needed relief to the
  area.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... Even less t-storms today with increasing chances 
for the new workweek. Turning hotter with high humidity continuing. 

Shortwave ridging building today as seen on water vapor channels
should inhibit thunderstorm for much of the area today. SPC DY1
outlook has cleared the northern half of the CWA from general
thunderstorms. Also, smoke is present over the area as seen on
GeoColor imagery.

As for Monday, the chances for thunderstorms have increased given 
another piece of shortwave energy ejecting across the region. 
Current 00z guidance suggests scattered to numerous thunderstorms 
across the region with a focus east of the Alleghenies Monday 
afternoon and evening. SPC currently has most of the region in a 
Marginal Risk (Level 1 out of 5) for severe weather with a Slight 
Risk (Level 2 out of 5) grazing northwest Garrett Co. MD. Machine 
guidance is also high on the severe threat with WxNext2 
probabilities of 30-60 percent and CSU probabilities of 15 to 30 
percent across the area during the Monday into Tuesday timeframe. 
Even with that said, coverage and timing remain the two big question 
marks similar to what we saw on Saturday across the region. With a 
hot and humid airmass in place and marginal shear this will be 
something to watch in the near term period. 

Additional shortwave disturbances look to pass through Tuesday into 
Wednesday and again Wednesday into Thursday. Uncertainty remains in 
regards to timing and coverage which will dictate the risk for 
severe weather. Current machine learning guidance and day 4-8 
outlooks from SPC mention at least a chance for severe weather each 
day mainly during the afternoon and evening hours. Ensemble and 
deterministic guidance put us in an MCS setup which will make it 
even harder to time out severe weather, especially with complexes of 
storms moving around the top of the ridge. Once again something that 
will continue to monitor in the coming days ahead. 

Outside of he storm chances expect highs in the upper 80s and low 
90s with heat indices east of the Blue Ridge up around 100 degrees. 
The hottest days look to be today and Monday given the strengthened 
subtropical ridge nearby. Highs will push into the mid 90s with heat 
indices closer to 105 degrees east of the Blue Ridge/along the urban 
corridor Monday afternoon.

KEY MESSAGE 2...A cold front could arrive late next week bringing 
relief from the heat and humidity into the upcoming weekend. 

Daily storm chances look to continue through at least Saturday as a 
more potent frontal system tracks toward the region. Ahead of that 
front will be several fast moving shortwave disturbances which will 
help aid in shower and thunderstorm development during the diurnal 
period. Storm coverage is a bit uncertain Thursday into late week as 
the front tries to push through. Speaking of the front, details 
still remain muddled on it's passage. Most 00z ensemble guidance 
suggests a frontal passage late Thursday into Friday while others 
have a front Friday into Saturday. Other deterministic members try 
to stall the front to the south Friday into Saturday while bringing 
it back north through the end of the weekend into early next week.

With that said, there is even more uncertainty in regards to severe 
weather Thursday through Saturday based upon cloud cover and the 
placement of the front. Of course any decent frontal passage we'll 
have to be monitor given machine probabilities remaining between 5-
15 percent for severe weather. Temperatures will cool from the 90s 
into the low to mid 80s late week. Overnight lows will fall back 
into the low to mid 60s with 50s over the mountains.

&&

.AVIATION /14Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Prevailing VFR conditions are expected across the terminals through 
at least Thursday given subtropical high pressure offshore and the 
lack of any real front passing through. Brief periods of sub-VFR are 
likely during the afternoon and evening hours due to thunderstorms.

Today will bring the least amount of t-storms between the terminals 
given a strengthened subtropical ridge over the region. An isolated 
shower or t-storm could pop up this afternoon west of MRB and south 
of CHO/SHD between 18z-00z/2-7pm. Coverage will be very isolated in 
nature with most seeing nothing at all. Winds will remain light out 
of the west and southwest at less than 15 kts.

Storm coverage increases Monday into Tuesday as another shortwave 
disturbance passes through. The risk for severe weather is also 
increasing during this time with a focus during the peak heating 
period 18z-01z/2-8pm Monday afternoon and evening. Storm coverage 
remains uncertain with gusty winds, frequent lightning, and locally 
heavy rainfall as the primary concerns. Similar conditions are 
expected Tuesday and Wednesday with restrictions possible in the 
afternoon and evening due to thunderstorms. 

Outside of the thunderstorms expect patchy fog between the terminals 
each morning through Friday. Winds will remain light out of the west 
and southwest at less than 15 kts. 

Temporary restrictions will continue at times due to showers and 
thunderstorms through at least Saturday as we await a cold front to 
sweep through.

&&

.MARINE...
Sub-SCA level winds are expected today with occasional gusts up
to 15 kts over the open waters of the Chesapeake and tidal 
Potomac. A brief period of southerly channeling may return to 
the open waters Monday afternoon and evening. Overall sub-SCA 
level winds are expected through Thursday morning. 

Outside of the background winds, expect daily shower and 
thunderstorm chances are each afternoon and evening through upcoming 
workweek. The least amount of coverage will be today with greater 
coverage Monday and Tuesday afternoon/evening. Special Marine 
Warnings may be needed to encompass any stronger thunderstorms that 
may form. Damaging wind gusts and frequent cloud-to-ground lightning 
will be the main threats between 19z-01z/ 3-9pm.

&&
